summary: `Table` type mismatch for set/elem/grow/copy/new operations not checked
description:
### Summary

A `table` can be either a `funcref` (a reference to a function), or on `externref` (external data pointer) and all the table-related operations must validate the table type.

### Details

```
  (module
    (table $table 0 1 funcref)
    (func (param externref) (result i32)
      (table.grow $table (local.get 0) (i32.const 1))))
...
(module
  (table $t 1 externref)
  (elem $e externref (ref.null extern))
  (func (export "_start")
    i32.const 0
    i32.const 0
    i32.const 1
    table.init $t $e))
```

### Proof of concept

Shown WAT snippets demonstrate.

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

### Impact

An attacker can potentially place a random address of a function pointer into a `funcref` Table and later use it as a target or an indirect call.
